title: Global Sensitivity Analysis of a Reactive Transport Model for Abiotic Trichloroethylene Reduction by Reduced Iron Minerals in Clay‐Rich Aquitards
content:
Abstract

Back-diffusion of trichloroethylene (TCE) from clay-rich aquitards poses a persistent challenge to groundwater remediation at many contaminated sites. Previous studies have demonstrated that natural attenuation of TCE is controlled by abiotic reactions with reactive ferrous iron; however, the coupled roles of mineral inventory, mineral reactivity, and biogeochemical processes governing reduced iron formation remain poorly understood. In this study, a global sensitivity analysis was performed on a reactive transport model using the Distance-based Generalized Sensitivity Analysis method to identify key parameters that control abiotic reduction of TCE in clay-rich aquitards under anoxic conditions. Uncertain input parameters including sediment composition, surface area, intrinsic reactivity, thermodynamics, and microbial kinetics were varied across plausible ranges, and model realizations were clustered based on quantities of interest related to TCE degradation and mineral phase evolution. Results show that TCE attenuation is controlled by the initial inventory, reactive surface area of reduced iron minerals and by their surface-area-normalized intrinsic reaction rates with TCE. Across most realizations, TCE attenuation in clay-rich aquitards can be effectively approximated as a first-order decay process when sufficient reactive iron is present. Secondary controls associated with biological iron and sulfate reduction processes influence TCE degradation only under a narrow subset of conditions characterized by limited initial reduced iron availability, where mineral regeneration becomes rate-limiting. These findings provide a quantitative basis for simplifying reactive transport representations of abiotic TCE degradation and highlight the conditions under which detailed biogeochemical coupling is necessary for reliable prediction of long-term abiotic natural attenuation of TCE in clay-rich aquitards.
